The randomized CADASIL trial compares a tocotrienol complex against vitamin-E-stripped soybean oil capsules. The target is clinical worsening in small-vessel disease and the primary analysis does not establish a between-group benefit. The source does not isolate a refined culinary soybean-oil effect versus no oil or report a Parkinson walking comparison.

The completed 20-participant dialysis pilot registers a combination of lentil flour, pea protein and micronutrients. Its primary measure is muscle mass. The linked original conference member reports protocol design and preliminary nutrition questionnaire information. The registry had no results posted on review. It does not test canned lentils or prespecify Parkinson walking slowness.

A completed 30-participant crossover registers a grapeseed-oil solution containing an additional component, saline and other comparisons for experimentally induced oral discomfort. Results were unposted at review. Processing grade is unreported and the oil cannot be separated from the additional component. This is a targeted pain-outcome gap rather than evidence for a clinical direction.

The published protocol specifies ginger as one odorant in a multiodor intervention for persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction. Registered outcomes concern olfaction, and the recruiting record had no results. The protocol and registry are one study family. It does not compare ingested grated ginger or Parkinson olfactory impairment.
